rows.evidence: Q1: ET-based scheduling and technology section, Eqs 1-8 and Table VI: authors compute net irrigation requirements and fraction of requirement (FIR) by crop, county and technology from Agri-Partners demonstration and TWDB data and run demand scenarios. Q2: Table VI and corn-to-cotton section: SDI cotton applied 274 mm with FIR 1.01 versus centre pivot 274 mm/FIR 1.03, with greater lint yield under SDI (1.48 vs 1.17 Mg/ha); authors state SDI may not necessarily result in less irrigation demand. Q6: FIR values are weighted averages across counties from about 450 commercial fields (20 000 ha) in the Northern High Plains Agri-Partners program. Q8: authors note Agri-Partners yields may reflect greater management level than USDA data, that TWDB volumes by technology were not available, and SDI share was assumed negligible in the scenario model.
rows.notes: Own SDI result is a single-crop (cotton) comparison of applied depth and yield from demonstration farms; it shows no reduction in applied water relative to centre pivot (only higher yield per unit water), so it does not clearly support the 'delivers water conservation' direction. Statements on SDI yield, WUE and soil temperature advantages are cited from other work (Bordovsky and Porter 2003; Colaizzi et al. 2004-2006), not own results. Single data source, no dispersion measures, no mechanism measured.

rows.evidence: Q1: Eqs 1-8, Table VI, Figures 7-8: own computation of Ireq, FIR and demand volumes. Q2: Table VI and text: FIR for fields managed with the TXHPET network (Agri-Partners) was generally lower than FIR from TWDB data for all crops, with yields seldom reduced; Figure 7 and conclusions: doubling TXHPET-managed area from 40% to 80% (with gravity reduced to 10%) computed to cut withdrawals by about 1 billion m3/yr (14%), up to 21% at full adoption. Q5: Table VI reports FIR with and without network management separately for six crops (corn, cotton, sorghum, peanut, soybean, wheat) and Figure 7 reports demand for Northern and Southern High Plains. Q6: results are for the 39-county Texas High Plains region and derived from 450 commercial fields; Figure 7 regional demand estimates. Q8: authors state Agri-Partners yields may reflect greater management than USDA county data, that TWDB demand by irrigation technology was unavailable, that the 40% adoption fraction is an estimate from subscriber counts, and that peanut Kc does not account for surface wetting needs.
rows.notes: Evidence is observational (applied depths from demonstration fields vs survey-based county volumes) fed into a demand model; comparison between Agri-Partners and TWDB data is the result itself, not independent triangulation. The intermediate variable (over-application relative to ETc requirement) is embodied in FIR but no separate mechanism (e.g. drainage, soil water) is measured. Scenario ranges of adoption are not uncertainty analysis; no SD/CI reported. Paper is partly a review of other strategies (Table IV from Amosson et al. 2005), which were not counted.

notes: The paper mixes a historical review of TWDB survey data with original analysis (computation of net irrigation requirements, FIR by crop and technology from Agri-Partners demonstration data, and regional demand scenarios). Only the original analysis was counted as own results. Full text appears complete.
